newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Schengen set start date for Austria, Italy, Greece.
newsitem.headline: Schengen set start date for Austria, Italy, Greece.

text.p: The Schengen group of seven European countries on Friday set a target date of October 26, 1997 for the full entry of Austria, Greece and Italy into its open-border pact.

The Schengen executive committee, meeting in Lisbon, said it would analyse whether the three countries will have security information systems in place to make the deadline at its next meeting on June 24.

The three have already signed but not fully implemented the Schengen accord which introduces passport-free movement across European frontiers. France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal and Germany are all full Schengen members.

"There is enormous political will to implement the Schengen timetable, but the checklist of requirements must be gone through," Portuguese Secretary of State for European Affairs Francisco Seixas da Costa told a news conference.
